- [EVENT] The user just got back from a surfing trip in San Diego.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] July is a great time to visit the Rockies, with warm weather and long days.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Daytime temperatures in July usually range from the mid-70s to mid-80s Fahrenheit (23-30°C) in lower elevations (below 8,000 ft).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] At higher elevations (above 8,000 ft), daytime temperatures can be 10-15°F (5-8°C) cooler.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nighttime temperatures can drop significantly, ranging from 50°F to 60°F (10-15°C).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] July is typically a dry month in the Rocky Mountains, with an average of 1-2 inches (2.5-5 cm) of precipitation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Afternoon thunderstorms are common in the Rockies during the summer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Humidity is usually relatively low in the Rockies, ranging from 30-50%.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] UV radiation is high at high elevations, so sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat are recommended.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wind can be a factor, especially in the afternoons, so packing layers is advised.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The weather can vary depending on the specific location within the Rocky Mountains.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The southern Rockies (e.g., Colorado, New Mexico) tend to be warmer and drier than the northern Rockies (e.g., Montana, Wyoming).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Higher elevations (e.g., above 10,000 ft) will be cooler and potentially snowier than lower elevations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended websites for specific weather forecasts include National Weather Service (NWS), OpenSnow, and Mountain-forecast.com.
- [EVENT] The user is planning to do some backpacking and camping in the Rockies.
